domain: F degrees of freedom above 1E10 (measured accuracy envelope; raised from 1E5 after CR-P1-02, benchmark/envelope_probe; the both-large orientation binds, crossing near df 1.5E5-3E5)
cause: incomplete-beta continued fraction loses accuracy while its local convergence test still passes
observed_effect: the original 1E5 boundary was measuring the CR-P1-02 prefactor cancellation rather than an intrinsic limit; re-measured in benchmark/envelope_probe the kernel is accurate to 5.1E-10 relative at df 1E10, and the public F surface now REJECTS df above PROB_F_MAX_DF with CVErr(xlErrNum)
notes: Strict validated-domain policy (PROB_F_ValidateEnvelope). F_Density carries its own separate envelope PROB_DENSITY_SHAPE_MAX (df above 1E20 rejected, benchmark/density_large_shape); it is not governed by the df caps above. Distinct from the LogBeta normalization defect.

domain: upper tail beyond the central region (standardized z above ~2.75-3.25)
cause: the standard-normal survival core loses RELATIVE accuracy in the deep tail (absolute error stays ~1E-17)
observed_effect: relative error grows monotonically: ~1E-14 at z=3, ~1E-13 at z=4, ~5E-11 at z=5, ~5E-10 at z=6
notes: Tight central contracts are domain-restricted accordingly. Still far better than 1-CDF cancellation; only the RELATIVE bound degrades, not the absolute.

domain: both shapes sufficiently small (roughly a, b below 1E-3), interior probabilities
cause: For sufficiently small positive Beta shapes the distribution becomes numerically indistinguishable in binary64 from a two-point limiting distribution with an interior CDF plateau approximately equal to b/(a+b). For some probabilities the mathematical quantile lies below the smallest positive Double or closer to one than the nearest representable interior Double.
observed_effect: No representable interior quantile or meaningful forward round-trip exists; e.g. at a=1E-12, b=9.9E-14 the interior CDF is flat at ~0.0901 across the whole representable interval and the p=0.5 quantile needs 1-x ~ 1E-1E13.
evidence: benchmark tiny_unbalanced_representable regime; the representable region is under a frozen tail-residual contract (Beta 1E-14), holdout-validated on independent interior points (worst 5.69e-15, 1.8x margin); points outside it have no representable quantile
notes: Floating-point representability boundary, NOT inverse-solver non-convergence. Value-accuracy contracts are scoped to the representable region; the collapsed region carries behavioral tests only.

domain: both degrees of freedom sufficiently small, interior probabilities
cause: F_CDF(x; d1, d2) = I_y(d1/2, d2/2), so small d1 and d2 inherit the Beta two-point collapse described in BetaInverse.InteriorQuantileRepresentability.
observed_effect: The interior CDF plateaus and the mathematical quantile leaves the representable Double range for probabilities away from the plateau.
evidence: benchmark tiny_unbalanced_representable regime; the representable region is under a frozen tail-residual contract (F 1E-13), holdout-validated on independent interior points (worst 7.08e-14, 1.4x margin)
notes: Same representability boundary as the Beta inverse, reached through the half-degree-of-freedom shapes.

domain: Student t degrees of freedom above 1E8 (measured envelope; raised from 1E6 after CR-P1-02, benchmark/envelope_probe)
cause: incomplete-beta tail loses accuracy while its convergence test still passes
observed_effect: measured 1.2E-09 relative at df 1E8 and degrading roughly tenfold per decade beyond; the public t surface REJECTS df > 1E8 with CVErr(xlErrNum)
notes: Strict validated-domain policy (PROB_T_ValidateEnvelope). StudentT_Density is unrestricted. Beyond ~1E15 the true t equals the normal to Double precision.

domain: Chi-square degrees of freedom above 1E8 (measured envelope; raised from 1E6 after CR-P1-02, benchmark/envelope_probe)
cause: incomplete-gamma path unvalidated beyond the cap and divergent at the top
observed_effect: measured 3.1E-11 relative at df 1E8; the P2-02 divergence at df 1E16 was the CR-P1-02 prefactor cancellation, not an intrinsic limit; the public chi-square surface REJECTS df > 1E8 with CVErr(xlErrNum)
notes: Cap at 1E8 because the lower-tail series reaches PROB_GAMMA_MAX_ITER above it - a reachability edge, not an accuracy one. ChiSquare_Density is closed-form and contract-frozen to shape 1E20.

domain: X below 3.854839696505424E-308, that is PROB_MIN_NORMAL / EulerGamma
cause: the leading term EulerGamma * X is itself subnormal, so the returned Double has no grid point near the answer
observed_effect: scaled absolute error grows toward the half-ulp bound 0.5 * minimum_subnormal / X: measured 1.92E-16 at X = 1E-308, 1.29E-14 at 1E-310, 1.41E-04 at 1E-320 and 4.18E-01 at the smallest positive subnormal
notes: Representability limit of the OUTPUT, not an algorithm defect: no evaluation order can place a value on a grid that has no point near it. The boundary is mathematical rather than empirical - measured error stays inside the small contract somewhat below it, but the quantization begins exactly where EulerGamma * X leaves the normal range. Measured is at or below the closed-form bound at every point, worst gap 11.7x at X = 1E-315. These points are deliberately excluded from LogGamma1p.small: pooling them would corrupt a contract whose evidence is the normal-result range.
